title: [Agent Lab] 3D dimensions map in the style of Google Earth
body:
### Task description

Add a 3D map view of the multiverse dimensions. It must look like Earth in Google Earth: a spherical globe with a real Earth texture that the user can rotate, zoom, and explore, with the dimensions/locations placed on it.
Original request: "a 3D map of the dimensions, the look must be like Earth in Google Earth."
Decisions confirmed by the requester:
- Locations are positioned deterministically (the same location always lands in the same spot).
- A real Earth texture is used.
- Adding a 3D library is allowed. The planner chooses it.
- The view coexists with the current 2D map and does not replace it.
- It must work on mobile/touch devices.
- The release uses a Blue/Green deployment controlled by a Feature Flag.
- This task must create the Blue/Green infrastructure and workflows, because they do not exist in the repo today.

Assumptions (to be confirmed): the same location data as the 2D map is used; there are no backend changes; the planner decides how the user switches between 2D and 3D.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A new view exists with a 3D globe using a real Earth texture (atmosphere/glow and a starry background).
- [ ] The texture and assets have a compatible free license, and attribution is documented.
- [ ] The user can rotate, zoom, and tilt the globe with a mouse (drag/wheel) and with touch (drag/pinch).
- [ ] Each loaded location appears as a marker on the globe at a deterministic position (a pure function with unit tests).
- [ ] Selecting a marker opens the location detail (reusing `LocationDetailPanel`).
- [ ] Loading, error, and empty states are shown (reusing `LoadingPortal`, `ErrorState`, `EmptyState`).
- [ ] The user can switch between the 2D and 3D maps, and the 2D map stays unchanged.
- [ ] The 3D view is behind a feature flag, off by default. With the flag off, the app behaves exactly as it does today.
- [ ] Blue/Green infrastructure is defined in `infra/` (Bicep), with two environments/slots and a traffic-swap mechanism.
- [ ] Workflows in `.github/workflows/` deploy to the inactive environment, verify it, then swap traffic. Rolling back is done by swapping again.
- [ ] The code ships via Blue/Green with the flag off. The flag is turned on later, independently of the deployment, and can be turned off immediately as a rollback.
- [ ] The Blue/Green procedure and the flag activation/rollback steps are documented (for example, next to `docs/canary-deployment.md`).
- [ ] Changes in `infra/` are validated (for example, `az bicep build`) and introduce no secrets into the repository.
- [ ] An accessible fallback is shown when WebGL is unavailable.
- [ ] The new 3D dependency is justified in the PR and lazy-loaded so it does not bloat the initial bundle.
- [ ] Frontend tests and lint pass.

### Scope - layers

- [x] Frontend (frontend/)
- [ ] Backend (backend/src/Favorites.Api, .Application, .Domain, .Infrastructure)
- [x] DevOps / Infra (.github/workflows/, infra/)

### Scope - exact paths/globs

Best guess, planner to confirm:

```
frontend/src/components/MultiverseGlobe*.tsx
frontend/src/components/MultiverseMapView.tsx
frontend/src/utils/globeLayout*.ts
frontend/src/types/view.ts
frontend/src/App.tsx
frontend/src/styles.css
frontend/src/services/featureFlags/**
frontend/public/** (Earth texture)
frontend/package.json
frontend/package-lock.json
infra/appservice.bicep
infra/main.bicep
.github/workflows/** (deployment workflows; exact files to be confirmed)
docs/** (Blue/Green and flag documentation)
```
